Print and plot selection probabilities

Source: R/plot.SelectionOC.R, R/print.SelectionOC.R
SelectionOC-methods.Rd

print() shows the probability that the decision rule selects each cohort, with one row per threshold and one column per cohort. plot() draws these probabilities against the threshold, one line per cohort, or as bars when there is a single threshold. Results of several statistics combined with rbind() are printed as a data frame and cannot be plotted together.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'SelectionOC'
plot(x, main = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'SelectionOC'
print(x, digits = 3, ...)

Arguments

x

Data frame returned by SelectionOC.

main

Title of the plot.

...

Not used.

digits

Number of significant digits.

Value

print() returns x invisibly. plot() returns invisibly the matrix of selection probabilities, with one row per threshold and one column per cohort.

See also

SelectionOC

Examples

set.seed(1)
res <- data.frame(sim = rep(1:200, each = 3), group = rep(c("A", "B", "C"), 200),
                  is_reference = rep(c(TRUE, FALSE, FALSE), 200))
res$ntb <- ifelse(res$is_reference, NA,
                  rnorm(600, rep(c(0, 0.05, 0.15), 200), 0.1))
oc <- SelectionOC(res, "ntb", threshold = seq(0, 0.3, by = 0.05))
oc
#> Probability that the rule selects each cohort
#> Statistic: ntb (Net treatment benefit against the reference)
#> 
#>  threshold     A     B     C
#>       0.00 0.010 0.290 0.700
#>       0.05 0.080 0.260 0.660
#>       0.10 0.205 0.205 0.590
#>       0.15 0.460 0.130 0.410
#>       0.20 0.680 0.050 0.270
#>       0.25 0.870 0.010 0.120
#>       0.30 0.935 0.000 0.065
plot(oc)
